title: Accuracy failure in reduction kernel
body:
This is another bug mimimized from our attempt to update PyTorch's triton pin in  pytorch/pytorch#109601. The minimized pytorch code is:
<details>

        stream0 = get_cuda_stream(0)
        triton_red_fused_0.run(arg0_1, arg1_1, buf1, 256, 128, grid=grid(256), stream=stream0)
        run_intermediate_hooks('sub', buf1)
        del arg0_1
        del arg1_1

def benchmark_compiled_module(times=10, repeat=10):
    from torch._dynamo.testing import rand_strided
    from torch._inductor.utils import print_performance
    arg0_1 = rand_strided((1, 16, 16, 128), (32768, 16, 1, 256), device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.float16)
    arg1_1 = rand_strided((1, 16, 16, 128), (32768, 2048, 128, 1), device='cuda:0', dtype=torch.float16)

    compiled_module_main('None', benchmark_compiled_module)

`git bisect` suggests that #2181 broke this kernel, and I see from the ttgir that different layout are used before and after the commit.

comments.body:
I tried the case with valid layout (4 warps / block):
```
BlockedLayout([1, 4], [8, 4], [4, 1], [1, 0], [1, 1], [1, 1], [0, 1]),
```
https://gist.github.com/participant4/f9f9b81af1c91b718a0544902feeb109 [llvm, ptx]
If I'm reading it correctly, in PTX we have:
```
@%p5 st.shared.b32 [ %r17 + 0 ], %r18; # ST1 (we have 8 of these)
...
setp.lt.s32 	%p13, %r42, 128; # p13 = tid.x < 128
...
@%p13 ld.shared.b32 %r33, [ %r34 + 0 ]; # load SMEM[tid.x * 4] (for tid.x < 128)
```
So we have 128 threads each loading 1xb32, and we have 8 of those b32 stores -> we load more than we store?
This is also present very early, right after  `ConvertTritonGPUToLLVM `:
```
    %1156 = llvm.inline_asm has_side_effects asm_dialect = att operand_attrs = [] "@$2 st.shared.b32 [ $0 + 0 ], $1;", "r,r,b" %1155, %1024, %1144 : (!llvm.ptr<i32, 3>, i32, i1) -> !llvm.void loc(#loc) # we have 8 of these
    ...
     %1203 = llvm.mlir.constant(128 : i32) : i32 loc(#loc)
    %1204 = llvm.icmp "slt" %1199, %1203 : i32 loc(#loc)
    %1205 = llvm.getelementptr %1132[%1199] : (!llvm.ptr<i32, 3>, i32) -> !llvm.ptr<i32, 3> loc(#loc)
    %1206 = llvm.inline_asm has_side_effects asm_dialect = att operand_attrs = [] "@$2 ld.shared.b32 $0, [ $1 + 0 ];", "=r,r,b" %1205, %1204 : (!llvm.ptr<i32, 3>, i1) -> i32 loc(#loc) # tid.x < 128
```
Edit: I miscounted the stores: **p5** is **tid.x < 4**, so it is 8 stores, each done by 4 threads -> 8*4 = 32
but still wrong right? Should match 128?

comments.body:
> `ld.shared.v4.b16 	{%f1, %f2, %f3, %f4},`

My guess is that it probably zeros out the *high* order bits of the destination registers and puts the loaded data into the low-order bits.  I'm told this is what it does if you do a `ld.b16 %b32reg`.

> If that results in the lower bytes of the float being set, it would mean a very small but non-zero value and indeed the output of the sum is rounded to -0.0000.

It's going to be a lot worse than that if we are loading an f16 and then shoving it into an f32 register without an explicit convert.  There's no way to interpret those bits as an f32 that will result in something sane.  (If it was bf16 instead, then you have some hope.)

What you've posted indeed looks like a bug in LLVM.  Let me poke around.

Huh. Looks like we've got the size right, at least. But I think it was supposed to be an extending load and it should've been `.f16`.
